item.title: South African Fuel Price Data (Free Download)
item.description:
Every weekday we read the Central Energy Fund’s daily fuel report and the official prices from the Department of Mineral and Petroleum Resources. We use them for our live fuel price tracker. The same numbers are free to download here, so you can check our work or use them in your own charts and projects.

Download

FileWhat’s in it
Daily forecast (CSV)One row per CEF report since 12 March 2026: the expected change for each fuel, how much comes from oil prices and how much from the rand, and the rand/dollar rate.
Official prices (CSV)Official inland and coastal prices for each monthly adjustment, from August 2026.
Latest forecast (JSON)Today’s forecast in one file: current and expected prices, inland and coastal. For apps and websites.
Column guide (text)Every column explained, in plain words.

The files update automatically on weekdays, usually by 11:00 and otherwise by 14:30. The links never change, so you can bookmark them or load them straight into a spreadsheet.

item.title: Contact Us
item.description:
The best way to reach us is by email:

salocalinfo@gmail.com

We read every message and usually reply within a few working days.

What to contact us about

  • Corrections: if a figure, date or step in one of our articles is wrong or out of date, please tell us which page and what needs fixing. We correct errors quickly and note the change on the page (see our corrections policy).
  • Questions and feedback about our guides, the fuel price tracker or the site.
  • Advertising and partnerships.

What we can’t help with

SA Local Info is an independent information site. We are not SASSA, the Department of Transport, a municipality or any other government body, so we cannot check your grant status, change your application or handle your licence or fine. For those, please contact the official department directly. We will never ask for your ID number, banking details or passwords.

item.title: Corrections Policy
item.description:
We work hard to be accurate, but mistakes happen and official information changes. When we find an error, or a reader tells us about one, we fix it as quickly as we can.

How we correct articles

  • Factual errors (a wrong amount, date, step or name) are fixed in the article, and we add a short, dated correction note at the end saying what changed.
  • New official information (for example a new grant amount or fuel price) is added to the article, and the Updated date under the headline changes.
  • Small fixes to spelling or wording that do not change the meaning are made without a note.

We do not quietly delete or rewrite information to hide a mistake.

item.title: Editorial Policy
item.description:
SA Local Info publishes practical, plain-English guides for people in South Africa: fuel price forecasts, SASSA grants, driving and vehicle licences, traffic fines and travel. This page explains how we work.

Who we are

SA Local Info is a small team based in Cape Town. Articles are published under the name SA Local Info rather than under individual names, and the team is responsible for everything on the site. You can read more about us.

item.title: South African E-Wallets Help SRD Recipients Receive Funds
item.description: In South Africa, clients who rely on receiving funds through the Cash Send service are being urged to collect their funds as soon as they receive an SMS with a voucher number for their chosen bank. But what if clients have been approved for COVID-19 SRD but no payment date is indicated on their January status or earlier months, and have selected to be paid through the Postbank or Cashsend? In this case, they are urged to open bank accounts and upload them on the system to fast-track payments.

item.title: Privacy Policy
item.description:
This policy explains what information is collected when you visit salocal.info (“SA Local Info”, “we”, “us”) and how it is used. We are based in Cape Town, South Africa, and follow the Protection of Personal Information Act (POPIA).

The short version

  • You do not need an account to use this site, and we never ask for your ID number, banking details or passwords.
  • We use Google Analytics to count visits and Google AdSense to show ads. Both use cookies.
  • We do not sell your personal information.
  • If you email us, we use your email only to reply to you.

Information we collect

When you browse the site. We do not ask you for any personal information. Like most websites, the services below automatically receive technical information such as your IP address, browser and device type, the pages you visit and how you arrived at the site.
